turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Hi! How are you doing these days?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: A bit tired today, but okay.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Our place is always a mess, and I want to pick a cleaning system that sticks.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Let me describe all the options before you comment.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: The first idea is a chore chart where each person gets assigned rooms that rotate every week.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Then there's doing fifteen minutes of tidying together every evening before dinner.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Option three is one big cleaning session every Saturday morning for the whole house.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And the last one is just hiring a cleaner to come every two weeks.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: And that's the last one. What do you think?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: The fifteen minutes every evening tends to work best, because the mess never piles up. A chore chart helps if people argue about who does what. The big Saturday session works, but it can eat your whole morning.
